title.narrative: Greener and Healthier Cities in Bahrain

description.narrative:
Cities across the Arab Gulf region have witnessed major urban changes and notable socio-economic transformation by virtue of the rapid urbanization of the region and climate change. The significant increase in population of the Kingdom of Bahrain, in tandem with the geographical limitations in terms of land size (765.3 km²), have put significant stress on the country’s resources and increased the need for collaborative work to meet the accelerating demands of the growing population.
Many efforts have been made by the Government in view of the urban and environment transformations of the last twenty years, reflecting the priorities set in the Sustainable Development Goals. The Bahrain 2030 National Planning Development Strategy, developed in 2007, guides the development new national infrastructure and is designed to address the role of sustainable land use development in generating a stable, predictable, and long-term economic growth. The Strategy addresses several issues including natural resource preservation, infrastructure development and housing reformation. It also highlights the lack of a strategic vision for green public spaces in Bahrain and deplores the limited access to public open spaces in relation to the size of the population, emphasizing the need for enhanced urban public spaces.
Most recently, Bahrain made additional and ambitious commitments to the global climate goals, and the shared responsibility the international community must ensure a green future for all. At 6th United Nations Climate Change Conference of the Parties (COP26), His Royal Highness Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, the Crown Prince and Prime Minister highlighted the Kingdom of Bahrain’s commitment to reaching net zero by 2060. In addition, by 2035, Bahrain will reduce emissions by 30 percent through decarbonization and efficiency initiatives and double the deployment of renewables from the targets we set at COP21. The 2035 targets also include carbon removal solutions by quadrupling mangrove coverage, doubling tree coverage in Bahrain, and directly investing in carbon capture technologies. A National Plan for Afforestation (2022 -2035) following the announcements at COP26 aims to increase the tree count from 1.8 million trees to 3.6 trees by 2035, 270,000 trees yearly.
In response to Bahrain 2030 National Planning Development Strategy and the most recent commitments to the climate goals, the Ministry of Works, Municipalities Affairs and Urban Planning set targets the to develop a comprehensive landscaping, afforestation and green public spaces plan through: - Development of a strategy of afforestation and beautification of main streets and intersections, through the formulation of a unified vision for the main streets and intersections, setting standards, conditions and foundations for increasing available green area and improving the level of afforestation and beautification in public sites. - Afforestation and beautification of public parks, gardens and residential areas: creating standards, conditions and principles to increase the green area and raise the level of afforestation and beautification in parks and public spaces. - Developing legislation and laws that contribute to increasing the intensification of urban agriculture and afforestation throughout the Kingdom. - Community Partnership – promoting initiatives and participation at the level of individuals, public and private sectors. Various initiatives have been launched to preserve and pay attention to afforestation and beautification, and to support and increase agricultural productivity. - Increasing the density and production capacities of nurseries - supporting and stimulating private nurseries: supporting and stimulating private and public nurseries for the production and provision of seasonal flowers, shrubs and trees suitable for the local environment.
To attain its vision of greening Bahrain, as well as to accelerate progress towards achieving the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, particularly SDG 11, the Government has requested the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) and the United Nations Food Agriculture Organization (FAO) to pool their skills and jointly develop and implement a technical assistance project.
The overall goal of the project is to promote the transition toward more sustainable urban systems, improve environmental quality by increasing quality and use of green public spaces with direct effects on health and wellbeing of the residents in the Kingdom of Bahrain. The project is expected to deliver a long-term vision and strategy for greening cities in Bahrain including short, medium and long-term plans of actions to increase and improve the quality of green public spaces.
Specific Objectives are: - Develop a vision and strategy for greening Bahraini cities and enhancing environmentally sustainable urban development; - Improve and increase the availability, quality, and use of urban green public spac
